batch: The 36 candidate commits resolve in ONE local git pass, not 36 API calls — which also removes the gh-axi 2KB field truncation risk entirely. All four pure functions (catch rule, keep rule, review-depth selector, Repairs-line parser) share ONE scoped vitest run per commit via `loop.py run --kind vitest` over the changed test files. The two document panels and the diff panels each launch their lenses in one batch. Genuinely isolated: the 3 measured case runs, because each one IS the per-case cost measurement the spend gate asks for, so averaging them into one batched run would destroy the number the user is being asked to approve.
critical_path: Spec -> spec panel (cap 2) -> plan -> plan panel (cap 2) -> implement -> diff panels (cap 4) -> merge both repos -> run 3 cases -> STOP at the spend gate. Only the document stages and the diff panels are genuinely ordered; everything else below runs off the critical path. Case harvesting is NOT on it and has already started: all 36 candidate commits were resolved locally before the spec was written.
drivers: Projected drivers, largest first. (1) DOCUMENT-STAGE ROUNDS. A serial document stage measured 9 rounds elsewhere against 4 for a panel, and the measured failure mode is buying prose rounds past the point where findings turn code-shaped — one such arc spent 5 document rounds and 0 lines of code, with round 4 minting round 5 blocking HIGH. THIS IS THE DRIVER BEING CUT, before anything is spent: both document stages are capped at 2 panels and carry an explicit leave-now rule on the first majority-code-shaped round. (2) Diff-panel repetition at roughly 138,355 tokens and 680 s per lens run; cut by the reviewed-baseline manifest above, which makes intervening panels delta-scoped. (3) The 3 measured case runs, projected from the same medians at about 415,000 tokens and 34 minutes total; NOT cut, because they are the deliverable the spend gate exists to price. Codex independently named (3) the largest QUANTIFIED driver and (2) the one to cut; it could not see that (1) is larger still, because the process description did not carry the 9-vs-4 and 5-rounds-0-code measurements.
parallel: Four streams run concurrently. (1) Case harvesting from local git history — already done for resolution and sizing, continues for per-case defect-location derivation — needs no review verdict and no plan. (2) The skill-repo track (pure functions, finding-outcome store, case runner) and (3) the product-repo track (cases, pull-request template, CI step) touch DISJOINT file sets in TWO DIFFERENT repositories, so `--write` serialisation per tree does not couple them and they implement at the same time. (4) Every review round is a 3-lens panel launched in one batch against a frozen snapshot sha, never a serial chain. Accepted from the Codex process critique (high, 0.91): harvesting is pulled fully off the critical path rather than sitting after the plan.
scope: No production runtime code is touched: the change is confined to `.review-eval/`, `.github/`, `scripts/` in the product repo and `skills/codex-converge/` in the skill repo. Therefore NO Playwright/UI lens and no live-page grounding is owed, and no e2e review is re-earned — the e2e suites stay valid because nothing they drive changes. Accepted from the Codex process critique (high, 0.94): a reviewed-baseline manifest is kept, so intervening panels read only the fix delta plus open findings and unchanged code is not re-verified round after round; exactly ONE final panel reads the full pinned BASE...HEAD range. Accepted (medium, 0.87): the round-1 necessity lens is handed the plan stage recorded necessity decision and asked only for implementation deviations from it, not to re-take the decision. Accepted (medium, 0.90): bidirectional spec-to-task traceability is required only of NORMATIVE and DECISION lines; the five-questions evidence answers are cited by an affected task or marked informational, so evidence lines do not mint artificial tasks.
stop: Bounded by an outcome table per capped stage, not by a round count alone — accepted from the Codex process critique (medium, 0.96), which correctly observed that a ceiling without a terminal disposition is not a bounded stop. SPEC (cap 2 panels): zero findings accepts; prose findings revise and re-panel within the cap; a majority code-shaped round LEAVES the document stage immediately and re-types those findings as plan tasks discharged in the same commit as the code; anything unresolved at the cap is written into the spec as a named open risk with its owner. PLAN (cap 2 panels): same table, plus the traceability pass must come back with an empty unmapped set for normative and decision lines. DIFF (cap 4 panels): stop when a scoped confirming panel raises NO new production-risk finding; a production-risk finding still open at panel 4 blocks the merge and is reported to the user rather than deferred by me, because critical and high are not mine to defer. The 3 measured case runs are themselves a hard stop written into the handoff: exactly 3, then report and wait.

note: The 9m55s solo wait was the round's last lens (spec-correctness-r2) finishing with the other two already returned, so there was no sibling lens left to overlap it with. The part that IS collectable forward is the NEXT stage's setup, and it was landed during that wait rather than after it: the track-S worktree at $HOME/Coding/claude-config-track-s was created and the 24-task implementation routing table was written into the tracked dispositions ledger while the lens ran. Landed as a schedule change for the plan panel: its two lenses launch concurrently against a frozen loop.py snapshot of the plan commit, and the Codex sibling worktree plus its node_modules symlink are provisioned during that wait. What is NOT removed is the gate itself - the plan panel is gated on close-round, which is gated on the last lens - because that serialisation is correctness-bearing and a lever may not buy speed by verifying less.

Declined on the measurement and on a repo-specific hazard. The run was 39.0s, LONE (0 of the slow ones overlapped another CPU job), which is the only reading that would justify touching compiler config - but 39s once per arc is not a bill worth paying for, and in THIS repository editing tsconfig.json is specifically hazardous: next dev's writeConfigurationDefaults appends a generated-types glob to tsconfig.json's include on every e2e boot (CLAUDE.md records it going from 3 entries to 107, 81 of them absolute paths into /var/folders), so the file is deliberately kept out of reach via typescript.tsconfigPath and assertTsconfigUntouched. Reconsider only if the implementation stage's repeated tsc runs become a measured cost, in which case the lever to pull is scoping the run, not changing the config.

Round 2 is launched on a frozen snapshot of 768d451d and track-S/track-P implementation runs underneath it, so the lens's wall-clock overlaps the fix stream instead of blocking it. Round 1's 5m34s blocking wait was the predecessor's; this window pays none.

Round 2's single lens ran on a frozen snapshot while S1 was implemented and committed in the other repository and Codex's P1 ran in a third worktree; three streams overlapped and the lens blocked nothing. The L1 evidence line counts the lens's own wall-clock as wait because loop.py cannot see work outside its ledger.
